module_role: Cross-sheet sequence, diagram, and BAS-network ground truth from M-801 through M-805. It records printed control behavior and explicit omissions without converting sequences to unsupplied final programming or installed I/O quantities.

network_architecture.BAS_role: Building automation system (BAS) receives/controls printed sequences and displays/alarms described on M-803 through M-805.
network_architecture.boiler_sequencing_controllers: Each boiler has a full-modulation sequencing controller capable of independent operation and interoperability with BAS.
network_architecture.lab_ahu_controller: Factory-installed unit-mounted independent DDC controller; M-804 expressly requires BACnet compliance and BAS/DDC interoperability.
network_architecture.airside_exhaust_controllers: M-804 says high-plume/exhaust factory DDC controllers are independent yet connected/interoperable with BAS using DDC.
network_architecture.explicit_BACnet_observation: M-803 diagram calls out an OA-duct reference temperature sensor over BACnet for OA temperature; M-804 calls the laboratory AHU controller BACnet compliant.
network_architecture.failure_mode: For the M-803 secondary chilled-water pumps, communications-network failure commands fixed pump speed.

heating_water_boiler_plant_M803: The hot-water plant is two boilers (B-1A/B-1B) and two VFD hot-water pumps (P-3A/P-3B) serving AHUs/roof-top-unit preheat coils and VAV reheat coils.
BAS/manual override can start and stop the hot-water plant; an adjustable one-minute delay plus differential-pressure proof precedes sequencing-controller enablement.
Pumps rotate weekly by least runtime; the lead isolation valve opens, lag isolation valve closes, one pump operates, and an alarming lead-pump failure starts the lag pump.
BAS uses current switches for proof and alarms if actual status departs BAS start/stop after the adjustable proving period.

VFD speed is controlled using DPS-1 sensed differential pressure against the DPS-2/DPS-3 desired setpoint; the TAB contractor supplies minimum-output-vector-graph settings for defined operating DP settings.
Boilers rotate weekly by least runtime. In remote, their sequencing controllers control boiler temperature/reset/firing/sequence; local leaves the boiler to internal control.
The lead boiler starts low-fire on low HWS temperature; 60% firing plus still-low HWS after adjustable 20 minutes enables the next boiler, while all enabled boilers modulate in parallel.
HWS reset uses TS-OA. Differential-pressure reset is 25 psi to 5 psi adjustable; coil-valve position determines the critical zone, with stated 85%, 95%, and 97% damper-position reset logic.

Gas pressure is displayed at BAS. A hardwired manual-mushroom emergency interface shuts down boilers independent of BMS programming and creates a BMS alarm. BAS sends variable HWS setpoint to each sequencing controller.
chilled_water_and_ice_storage_M803: The chilled-water system is manually started and runs continuously.
The lead primary pump runs continuously with the lead chiller; failure starts the second pump/alarm and supports manual or timed lead rotation.

A differential-pressure sensor at each chiller measures evaporator supply-to-return drop; active-chiller pressure controls primary-pump speed. When both chillers run, both signals are averaged and both primary pumps run in tandem.
Chiller isolation opens before differential-pressure-switch flow proof enables internal controls; manufacturer controls operate compressors/condenser fans while DDC can adjust power-limit setting.

Secondary pumps start continuously, use a 4-20 mA DC VFD speed command, operate in unison to maintain differential pressure, stage on low DP, and start the next pump on failure/alarm. Communication failure fixes pump speed.
V-2 keeps secondary CHW no colder than 5.5 C; it closes to the secondary circuit when both secondary pumps are off, bypassing primary water back to the chiller.
The load monitor uses secondary CHW flow plus building supply/return temperature.

Ice modes are make ice, use ice, and bypass. Make ice needs low-demand billing and inventory no greater than 80%; use ice needs high-demand billing, inventory greater than 25%, and at least one secondary pump. All modes may be commanded from the operator workstation.

In make-ice mode, the lead primary pump/chiller run and V-1 opens to storage; storage discharge reaches -2.2 C before change to use-ice or bypass. In use-ice mode V-1 maintains 5.5 C primary supply. In bypass V-1 closes to storage; both primary pumps/chillers stop if both secondary pumps stop.
laboratory_airside_M804: Laboratory AHUs 1, 2, 4 and 5 have factory-installed independent DDC, unit-mounted controller, BACnet-compliant BAS interoperability, hand-off-auto on major equipment, 15-minute analog trending, status change-of-value trending, 60-day archive, and dynamic color display.

AHU start/stop is time-of-day program logic with controller/BAS override. CHW/HW valves reset discharge-air temperature from outdoor air conditions. Supply fans run continuously and VFDs maintain static pressure.

Supply/exhaust static reset uses VAV damper positions: 95% open causes upward reset and less than 85% open causes downward reset at stated adjustable five-percent/ten-minute bands; initial static setpoint is 1.5 in wg adjustable.
Freeze protection is a hardwired low-limit switch interlocked with VFD: low limit trip closes OA damper, drives valves fully open, alarms BAS, and requires manual reset.

High-plume and general laboratory exhaust have factory DDC controllers, daily fan alternation, at least one operating fan, pressure-based fan staging, automatic-damper proof before full VFD ramp, and a 3,500 fpm minimum discharge-velocity control target.

M-802 supplies the laboratory/chemistry-room VAV and fume-hood logic: the hood controller uses sash position/face velocity/exhaust airflow; the room controller uses the total hood-exhaust setpoint, supply-valve flow and room temperature to maintain air-flow tracking differential, room pressurization and temperature with PID loops. The points are remotely monitored/controlled through the BAS.

M-804 covers fan-coil, laboratory AHU, hood/general-exhaust control diagrams and five printed I/O matrices. Its 42 source rows and their printed AI/DI/AO/DO matrix circles are captured separately in points_m804_m805; matrix rows are not an installed terminal total.
administration_airside_M805: M-805 provides administration AHU-3/AHU-6, return-air VAV, unit-heater, fume-hood/BIO-safety-cabinet alarm, mechanical-room exhaust, and stair-ventilation sequences plus the administration AHU and VAV I/O matrices.

Administration AHU logic provides morning warm-up/pre-cool, optimum start/stop, timed override, occupied/unoccupied modes, supply-duct-static reset using VAV-damper position, ventilation flow/setpoint logic, preheat/cooling valve control, return-fan static control, airflow monitoring, hardwired freezestat action, smoke shutdown and listed fan/filter/CO2/humidity/mixed-air alarms.

The printed VAV reheat sequence uses local space temperature, supply-air volume modulation, HWS reheat-valve control, occupied/unoccupied/morning-warm-up logic and ventilation/economizer context. The unit heater starts its fan/opens HWS valve at the adjustable thermostat condition; mechanical-room exhaust proves the damper open before its exhaust fan energizes.

All 33 M-805 matrix rows and their printed AI/DI/AO/DO category circles are captured in points_m804_m805. The 25 AI, 8 DI, 10 AO and 2 DO circles are logical matrix assignments, not an installed controller I/O-card/terminal count.
